messages:
maya: quick pulse — I ran the candidate pass for 'orca-lite-30b' overnight and the eval deck shows a small but consistent drop on socratic-code (~2.4% abs). not catastrophic but worth triage.

jordan: ugh. is that across quant configs? which one did you use? :thinking_face:

maya: baseline fp16 + int8-ptq (per-sample calibration). drop appears on both int8 and fp16 but bigger on int8.

sanjay: can you paste the exact eval row? also which prompt templates?

maya: paste from CSV: `socratic-code, promptset v3, fp16: 83.6, int8: 81.2`

elena: thanks — looks like a behavior shift on code generation. could be tokenizer differences or sampling seeds. did you run nll/regression tests?

maya: ran perf smoke + regression harness — no runtime errors. latency ~stable. attaching quick diffs in the doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/rd/eval-gap/orca-lite-30b-diff (private)

jordan: can we score this against our prioritization rubric? quick pass: user-impact medium, infra-risk low, rollout-cost medium, data-sensitivity low. I get a raw score 6/10.

sanjay: for roadmap alignment, this model unlocks smaller-device deployments which our infra PM wanted this quarter. that nudges priority up.

elena: propose action items: 1) run deterministic seeding + 3 seeds on the socratic deck 2) rerun with tokenizer sanity check (compare token counts) 3) try quant-aware finetune / bias-correct for int8 4) if still negative, fallback to fp16 for code routes.

maya: starting seeds now. queued three runs: tags `orca-lite-prio-2415` in CI. ci-bot: tests queued (job 4829).

ci-bot: CI update: job 4829 started on runner gpu-small-3. estimated 2h.

jordan: note for prioritization board — if quant-aware-finetune needed, estimate 2-3 engineer-weeks. flagging for roadmap review tomorrow.

elena: ok. can someone update the intake card with score rationale + links? maya, can you add the CSV + diff link to the card and set status = "investigating"?

maya: done. intake card: https://kanban.redwood.ai/board/ML-Onboard/INT-9823. status updated.

sanjay: after CI finishes, let's reconvene in async thread with pinned numbers. if we still see >1.5% regression on median we escalate to a canary hold.

jordan: agreed. also adding a quick metric to console: per-route fallback ratio for code endpoints so we can monitor in prod if we enable fp16 fallback.

elena: thanks all. small follow-up — if quant-finetune gets green, can we schedule a canary for dedicated next week? need to sync with infra.

maya: noted, will coordinate with infra and tag infra-oncall.

sanjay: small note for scoring: add a "rollback complexity" axis to the rubric — this one has moderate rollback complexity.

jordan: good call. adding that to the rubric doc now. https://docs.redwood.ai/rd/prioritization/rubric

elena: closing loop: keep thread updates short, tag #eng-oncall if we need capacity. will check back after CI. :white_check_mark:
